Pepper bell|Bacterial spot.symptoms: Small water-soaked spots that turn dark brown, often with a yellow halo; leaves yellow and drop.
Pepper bell|Bacterial spot.solution: Remove and bin infected leaves. Water at the base, never overhead, and don't handle plants when wet. A copper-based bactericide used exactly as labeled can slow spread. Rotate crops next season.

Pepper bell|healthy.solution: Keep watering at the base, give good airflow, and check leaves weekly.

Potato|Early blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings on older, lower leaves; leaves yellow and die.
Potato|Early blight.solution: Remove affected lower leaves, mulch to stop soil splash, water at the base and keep plants well fed. Use a fungicide labeled for potatoes if it keeps spreading. Rotate crops.

Potato|Late blight.symptoms: Dark water-soaked patches that spread fast, white fuzzy growth under leaves in humid weather.
Potato|Late blight.solution: Act quickly: remove and destroy infected plants (do not compost), avoid wet foliage, and use a protective fungicide labeled for late blight. Remove volunteer potatoes.

Potato|healthy.solution: Keep foliage dry, hill soil around plants, and inspect regularly.

Tomato|Bacterial spot.symptoms: Small dark greasy spots on leaves, sometimes with yellow halos; rough scabby spots on fruit.
Tomato|Bacterial spot.solution: Remove infected leaves, avoid overhead watering and working among wet plants, use a copper-based product as labeled, and rotate crops. Use clean seed.

Tomato|Early blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves, yellowing around them.
Tomato|Early blight.solution: Remove affected lower leaves, mulch, water at the base, stake plants for airflow, and use a labeled fungicide if needed. Clear plant debris at season end.

Tomato|Late blight.symptoms: Large dark water-soaked patches on leaves and stems, white mold underneath in humid weather, firm brown fruit rot.
Tomato|Late blight.solution: Spreads very fast. Remove and destroy infected plants (do not compost), keep foliage dry, and use a labeled protective fungicide on healthy plants nearby.

Tomato|Leaf Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow patches on upper leaf surfaces with olive-gray mold underneath; common in humid, poorly ventilated spaces.
Tomato|Leaf Mold.solution: Improve ventilation and lower humidity, space and prune plants, remove affected leaves, and water at the base. Use a labeled fungicide if severe.

Tomato|Septoria leaf spot.symptoms: Many small round spots with dark borders and gray centers, starting on lower leaves.
Tomato|Septoria leaf spot.solution: Remove spotted lower leaves, mulch to stop splash, water at the base, and use a labeled fungicide if it keeps spreading. Rotate crops and clear debris.

Tomato|Spider mites Two spotted spider m.symptoms: Fine yellow stippling on leaves, fine webbing, leaves drying out; worse in hot, dry conditions.
Tomato|Spider mites Two spotted spider m.solution: Spray leaves (especially undersides) with water, then use insecticidal soap or neem oil as labeled. Raise humidity, avoid dusty or drought-stressed plants, and isolate badly affected plants.

Tomato|Target Spot.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings, similar to early blight, sometimes on stems and fruit.
Tomato|Target Spot.solution: Remove affected leaves, improve airflow, avoid wet foliage, clear debris, and use a labeled fungicide if needed.

Tomato|Tomato YellowLeaf Curl Virus.symptoms: Small, yellowing leaves curling upward, stunted plants, poor fruit set. Spread by whiteflies.
Tomato|Tomato YellowLeaf Curl Virus.solution: No cure. Remove and destroy infected plants, control whiteflies (yellow sticky traps, fine mesh netting, insecticidal soap), and choose resistant varieties next time.

Tomato|Tomato mosaic virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green leaves, distorted or fern-like growth, stunted plants.
Tomato|Tomato mosaic virus.solution: No cure. Remove infected plants, wash hands and disinfect tools, avoid handling tobacco before touching plants, and use resistant varieties and clean seed.

Tomato|healthy.solution: Keep watering at the base, give good airflow, and check leaves weekly.
